papers.title: Relative Derived Torsion in Categories of Reduced Modules: Comparison and Non-Noetherian Examples
papers.abstract: Let $I$ be an ideal of a commutative ring $R$. We use relative derived torsion in exact full abelian subcategories of $I$-reduced modules to study ambient derived ideal-power torsion. Exact inclusion forces $IM=I^2M$ whenever $I^2$ is finitely generated. Over a Noetherian ring, every finite object consequently decomposes into its torsion part and $IM$, and its positive-degree ambient cohomology vanishes. For $R=S[t]$ and $I=JS[t]+(t)$ with $J^2=J$, we compute every stage of the canonical Ext system and its transition maps, obtaining a comparison with $\Ext_S^q(S/J,-)$. Valuation-domain and product-of-fields examples yield nonzero cyclic first cohomology. A further construction has cyclic coefficients and cyclic ambient cohomology in every positive even degree, while its positive-degree relative cohomology vanishes. Applications determine kernels of canonical Ext maps for these coefficient modules and identify the obstruction to ring-valued specialization in the questions of Eisenbud, Musta\c{t}\u{a}, and Stillman.

papers.title: Splitting module-finite extensions over singular local rings
papers.abstract: We study when a module-finite extension of a singular local ring splits as a module over the base. On a Gorenstein curve of positive residue characteristic, weak normality forces splitting for every extension of finite projective dimension. In residue characteristic two the converse holds when two is zero or a nonzerodivisor. A missing square root in the prescribed base gives an explicit nonsplit extension of generic rank four. We obtain a second curve criterion by gluing retractions on the branches and determine all evaluation ideals for coordinate crossings and for \(x^2=y^2u z_1\cdots z_s\) in odd characteristic. For cubic extensions we prove a presentation theorem with arbitrarily many relations. It applies on the blow-up of an ideal generated by a regular sequence of length three, and on the blow-up of a three-dimensional local ring with a quadric tangent cone. A family of matrices satisfying the criterion exists over every residue field in the regular-sequence case.

papers.title: Multivariate diagonal harmonics: character polynomials and proofs of two conjectures of Bergeron
papers.abstract: We prove Bergeron's Hook-Components and Coefficient-Length conjectures for the Vandermonde polarization module and full diagonal harmonics in every rank and number of alphabets. Hook-label characters are elementary skewings of the alternating character, and the maximal Schur length in label $\mu$ is $n-\mu_1$. We compute character and dimension polynomials of diagonal coinvariants in every bosonic--fermionic superspace for $D\ge3$, $n\ge\max\{D,2D-6\}$, answering Church--Ellenberg--Farb's character and dimension questions. For augmented commutative algebras in characteristic zero, we construct natural two-Schur presentations and filtered free resolutions with one Schur generator in each homological degree. For polynomial algebras, specialization to orthogonal idempotents identifies the first unstable correction for every nonempty tail $\tau$ and degree $D>|\tau|$. The stable threshold $n\ge D+\tau_1$ is sharp when the row dimension is at least $\ell(\tau)$. First parabolic algebras recover finite jets, their multiplication and their maps. Selected-label lifts give uniform Vandermonde generation through degree $D$ for $D\ge3$, $n\ge2D-3$, and disjoint-label products generate every first occurrence for positive integral row weights. Constructive degree reflection determines all two-column moment homology and generates its first syzygies from degree $n+1$; two-column Vandermonde generation reduces to degree $n-1$. Invariants and harmonics separate through the character range and through degree $n$ in two alphabets. The hook identities also give the fully graded sign component of the $t=0$, $(1,2)$-superspace Theta conjecture.

papers.title: Closed layers in tensor-triangular geometry
papers.abstract: In the absence of a theory of closed immersions in tensor-triangular geometry, we propose an alternative approach via quotients of module categories. As an application, we prove invariance of homological residue fields under completion.

papers.title: Representations of the quantum double of the restricted quantum group $\mathbf{\overline{u}}_q(\mathfrak{sl_2})$
papers.abstract: Let $q$ be a primitive $2p$-th root of unity with $p\ge2$, and let $H=D(\mathbf{\overline{u}}_q(\mathfrak{sl_2}))$ be the Drinfeld double of the restricted quantum group $\mathbf{\overline{u}}_q(\mathfrak{sl_2})$. We describe the dual Hopf algebra and the cross relations of $H$. A change of generator gives a classification of the simple $H$-modules. Their isomorphism classes are indexed by $\mathbb Z_{2p}^{\,2}$. We construct their projective covers, compute their dimensions, and determine which simple modules are projective. Finally, we prove that $H$ is strictly wild for every $p\ge2$ by constructing a fully faithful exact functor from finite-dimensional $\Bbbk\langle x,y\rangle$-modules to finite-dimensional $H$-modules.

papers.title: A conditional proof of the Casas-Alvero conjecture
papers.abstract: The Casas-Alvero conjecture states that if $f(X)$ is a monic univariate polynomial of degree $d$ over a characteristic $0$ field $\mathbb{K}$ such that $\gcd(f, f_{i})$ is non-trivial for each $i=1, \dots, d-1$, then $f(X)=(X-\alpha)^d$ for some $\alpha\in \mathbb{K}$. In this paper, we prove the Casas-Alvero conjecture for polynomials of any degree $d\geq 3$ over any characteristic $0$ field, under a uniform local {\L}ojasiewicz type hypothesis for a family of polynomials obtained from the elementary symmetric functions. Furthermore, we prove this estimate on compact subsets of a common Zariski open set of coefficients parametrizing the family.

papers.title: Computing weighted sheaf cohomology using noncommutative differential modules
papers.abstract: We describe a novel method for computing sheaf cohomology over weighted projective spaces and stacks using exterior algebra and differential module techniques, generalizing an algorithm due to Eisenbud-Fl{\o}ystad-Schreyer over projective space.

papers.title: The Kemper--Malle conjecture and isolated linear quotient singularities
papers.abstract: We prove the Kemper--Malle conjecture, which provides a modular analogue of the Chevalley--Shephard--Todd theorem. As a consequence, the classification of isolated linear quotient singularities over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic reduces to the classical Zassenhaus--Vincent--Wolf classification.
